findings.claim: The Claude Code sign-in flow B5.5 builds can never report success, because §6.3 maps the OAuth result of `claude auth login --console` to a state §6.4 declares unusable.
findings.evidence: §6.3 table: "`api_key`, `api_key_helper`, `third_party` → **usable**; `claude.ai`, `oauth_token` → **SubscriptionDeclined**" — but §6.4 says MailCraft "spawns `claude auth login --console`" and then "Success means `authMethod` is in the allow-list. A resulting `claude.ai` method is reported as declined.", i.e. the Console login it starts produces `oauth_token`, which §6.3 already labels SubscriptionDeclined. The poll in §6.4 ("every 2 s for up to 10 minutes") therefore always times out, and a legitimate API-billed Console sign-in is reported to the owner as the forbidden subscription case.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the mapping: distinguish a Claude.ai/Pro-Max subscription credential from an API-billed Console OAuth credential by the fields `claude auth status` actually emits (e.g. `accountRole`/billing type), and state the exact predicate that makes one usable and the other `SubscriptionDeclined`; add that predicate to SCN-RT-AUTH-001 and to SCN-RT-AUTH-001's post-login fixture set.

findings.claim: The terminal-error rule for SIWC refresh treats every 4xx as fatal, so a 429/408 rate limit permanently destroys the owner's ChatGPT sign-in, and SCN-RT-SIWC-002 asserts that wrong behaviour as correct.
findings.evidence: §6.2 Refresh: "A **4xx** from the token endpoint is **terminal**: delete the entry, set status `SignInEnded`, turn the runtime off"; SCN-RT-SIWC-002: "4xx terminal clears the entry and disables; a 5xx retries". 429 (rate limit) and 408 are 4xx, so a transient throttle deletes `ai.chatgpt`, disables the runtime and signs the owner out with "OpenAI ended this sign-in".
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict terminal handling to the OAuth grant errors the spec intends (e.g. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_client` and explicit revocation responses); classify 408/429 and other 4xx as transient with backoff. Add a negative-control fixture to SCN-RT-SIWC-002 asserting that a 429 keeps the entry and retries.

findings.claim: The SIWC client id has two mutually exclusive delivery mechanisms and no configuration surface, so the G-RT3 escape ("hidden until a client id is configured") cannot be implemented as written.
findings.evidence: §6.2: "The client id ships in the binary." vs B5.7: "hidden until a client id is configured (G-RT3)" and G-RT3 (a): "B7 code ships, runtime hidden until a client id is configured". `ai.json` v3 (§3) has no client-id field, §10 has no command to set one, and a public PKCE client id that ships in the binary cannot later be "configured".
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one: either the id is a build-time constant and the runtime is gated on "id != placeholder at build time", or add a documented `ai.json`/credential entry and a §10 command for the client id (with the same hostile-input checks as paths).

findings.claim: G-RT11 (a) recommends adding an "Anthropic API" runtime as "compat-style", but `compat:*` is defined as OpenAI-compatible and cannot carry the Anthropic Messages API wire format, and the runtime appears in no goal, spec section, change or default.
findings.evidence: §2: "`compat:<provider-id>` ... **Where** ... from the provider kind" over "`ProviderConfig` ... unchanged ProviderConfig list for compat:*" (§3) and §1 "OpenAI-compatible providers (what exists today)", while B3 G-RT11 says "(a) also add \"Anthropic API\" as a compat-style runtime". §1 lists "Seven runtime types" with no Anthropic entry; no B5.x change, §13 scenario or §8 default mentions it.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop G-RT11 (a), or spell it out as a new adapter (its own `crates/ai` module, recipe, `Where` = `leaves`, credential entry `ai.anthropic_api`, fuzz target, scenario) and add it to §1's list, §2, B5 and §13 so the count and the chain types stay consistent.

findings.claim: The owner's requested deliverable "KBD prompts guiding a different Claude Code (Opus 5.5) agent" is still owned by no change and the two plan sections disagree on where the prompts live.
findings.evidence: B0: "**Prompts:** `prompts/`" vs B9: "`docs/design/prompts/` updated if the phase changed anything they say (gate answers, change ids, scenario ids)"; B5.12 (`ai-runtime-docs`) covers only "PRIVACY.md, threat-model, docs/log.d + release-notes fragments, docs/mcp.md". The goal ("an updated PLAN.md and KBD prompts guiding a different Claude Code (Opus 5.5) agent") is therefore delivered by a conditional DoD line against an ambiguous path, with no change that produces the files.
findings.suggested_fix: State the real path once (B0 and B9), name the exact prompt files, and put the update in a B5 change (B5.12) rather than a conditional DoD line.

findings.claim: B10 redefines Part A's status chip (A 5.4) state vocabulary but no scenario asserts it, so the change is untestable as specified.
findings.evidence: B10: "A 5.4 (status chip) reads chain semantics after B. Its states become: \"AI off\" ... \"AI: on this computer\" ... \"AI: may leave for ‹accounts›\". B5.11 owns this update." The §13 table contains SCN-RT-BADGE-001 ("Part A narrowing badge (A 5.7) names the runtime") but nothing for the chip's three states or the "how many are ready" summary chip in §11.
findings.suggested_fix: Add SCN-RT-CHIP-001 asserting the three chip texts for: no enabled runtime, only local runtimes, and a consented `leaves` runtime (plus the no-consent case), and reference it from B5.11.

findings.claim: The `ask` and `stop` fallback policies in §9 have no acceptance scenario; only the `next` path is exercised, so the owner-facing error behaviour is untested.
findings.evidence: §9.2–3 define `next`, `ask` ("show '‹A› couldn't answer (‹reason›). Try ‹B›?'") and `stop` ("show the error"), and `ai.setFallback` accepts all three (§10), but §13 has only SCN-RT-CHAIN-001 ("the next eligible one answers") and no scenario naming `ask` or `stop`.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend SCN-RT-CHAIN-001 (or add SCN-RT-CHAIN-002) to run the same failing chain under `ask` and `stop`, asserting the prompt text/"show the error" and that no second run starts.

findings.claim: The G-RT0 (b) escape hatch (do Part B first) only accounts for re-planning A 5.4, although B5.11 and B5.10 also modify A 5.7 and A 5.6, which would not exist yet.
findings.evidence: B0: "If the owner wants B first, A 5.4 must be re-planned against the chain model (gate G-RT0)." vs B5.11: "status chip update (Part A 5.4); narrowing badge names the runtime (Part A 5.7, SCN-RT-BADGE-001)" and B5.10: "provenance list in the answer pane (extends child task 6.6)" / B10: "A 5.6 provenance gains the failed-runtime list (B5.10)".
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the G-RT0 (b) condition to A 5.4, A 5.6 and A 5.7 together, or state that option (b) is only available if Part A's 5.6/5.7 land first.

findings.claim: The v2→v3 migration table now has two rows that both claim to handle `primary: None` with opposite outcomes, and it has no row for an absent/null backup.
findings.evidence: §3.1: "primary explicitly None | chain with every entry disabled; `never_configured: false`" versus "`backup: "<provider id>"` ... → an enabled `compat:<id>` entry placed right after the primary's position (**or first, if the primary was None**)" and "`backup: "apple-on-device"` + confirmed `on_device` binding | `chain[1] = on_device`, enabled". A v2 file with `primary: null` and a backup therefore yields either a fully disabled chain or an enabled backup entry depending on which row wins; nothing covers `backup: null`/absent.
findings.suggested_fix: State precedence explicitly (backup rows win over the "every entry disabled" row, or the reverse), add a row for `backup: null`/absent, and cover all four combinations in SCN-RT-MIGRATE-001.

findings.claim: The hostile-input rules for `ai.json` v3 itself have no scenario, unlike the v2 migration and path-override rules, so "unknown runtime kinds dropped (never taken as local)" is unverified.
findings.evidence: §3: "size cap 256 KB; unknown runtime kinds dropped (never taken as local); every field checked" — but §13 has SCN-RT-PATH-001 (path overrides) and SCN-RT-MIGRATE-001 ("malformed v2") only, with no fixture for a malformed/oversized v3 file, an unknown `runtime` string, or a v2/v4 `version` value.
findings.suggested_fix: Add SCN-RT-SETTINGS-001 covering: a >256 KB file, an unknown runtime kind in `chain`, a bad `version`, and junk in `consents`/`keys_kept_for`, asserting the file loads safely, the unknown entry is dropped and never resolves to `local`, and nothing panics.

findings.claim: B5.4 schedules process-group kill, Windows job objects and AppContainer/Landlock containment in a workspace where `unsafe` is forbidden, without naming the safe boundary that makes that buildable.
findings.evidence: Constraints: `no-unsafe` — "'unsafe_code = \"forbid\" across the workspace; no unsafe blocks'" (blocking, `cargo check`), plus `quality-gate-passes`. B5.4: "process-group kill, spawn-time executable checks, **OS sandbox profiles (Seatbelt / Landlock / AppContainer)**" and §7.1: "Cancel kills the **whole process group** (Unix `setsid` + `killpg`; Windows job object)" — Win32 job objects and AppContainer are unsafe FFI, and no B3 gate, B6 wave note or §4 layering row says whether this comes from a safe wrapper dependency or requires a lint exception.
findings.suggested_fix: State per platform which crate supplies the safe API (e.g. `nix` for `setsid`/`killpg`, a safe job-object/AppContainer wrapper) and add a gate/verification item that resolves it before W2; if a lint carve-out is needed, record it as a decision against `no-unsafe` instead of discovering it at `cargo xtask ci`.

findings.claim: Two invocation details the recipes freeze are still marked "verify", so a failed verification silently changes the containment contract after the changes are scoped.
findings.evidence: §7.1: "passed by path (e.g. `--system-prompt-file`; **verify** the flag at assess), or prepended to stdin when no file flag exists" and §7.4: "a policy overriding project config (verify the env var that points OpenCode at it)", while §7.2 already hard-codes `--system-prompt-file <run-dir>/instructions.txt` and B5.5/B5.8 are scheduled in W3 from these recipes; §7.1's `sandbox-exec` note ("verify it is still usable for this at assess") is likewise already assigned to B5.4 in W2.
findings.suggested_fix: List these three verifications in the assess/analyze wave's explicit verification items (B6 row 1) and make B5.4/B5.5/B5.8 entry criteria depend on their outcome, so the fallback to stdin or to G-RT5 (b) is decided before the change is written.
